nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong summer sun and dry air shape the semi-desert, steppe and juniper slopes of the reserve.

nodes.name: Snow and snowmelt
nodes.desc: The reserve climbs from about 700 m to 2,800 m, so winter snow and spring melt water the upper slopes and meadows.

nodes.name: Stony mountain soil
nodes.desc: Thin, rocky soils on dry slopes hold the steppe, juniper and oak communities, which cover the reserve in altitude bands.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Steppe grasses
nodes.desc: Wild goatgrasses and other grasses grow on the dry steppe and meadows, which together are a large part of the reserve.

nodes.name: Juniper
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the reserve in sparse stands at mid altitude. Cinereous vultures nest on the old trees.

nodes.name: Caucasian oak
nodes.desc: Forms the oak woodland at higher elevations, producing acorns and shade for the forest community.

nodes.name: Wild pears
nodes.desc: The reserve is home to several wild pear species, including ones named after the area, whose fruit feeds many animals.

nodes.name: Bezoar ibex
nodes.desc: A wild goat of rocky mountain slopes that feeds on plants. It is a main prey of the big cats and wolves of the region.

nodes.name: European hare
nodes.desc: Grazes grasses and herbs in open ground and is eaten by foxes, eagles, lynx and wolves.

nodes.name: Common vole
nodes.desc: A small grass-eating rodent of open ground, the staple prey of many small predators.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats acorns, fruit, roots and other foods in the reserve.

nodes.name: Chukar
nodes.desc: A ground-nesting partridge of dry rocky slopes that eats seeds and plant matter.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A flexible hunter and fruit eater that takes voles, hares, birds and wild pears.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: A secretive cat of the reserve that hunts hares and ground birds.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A large raptor of open mountain country that hunts hares and game birds such as chukar.

nodes.name: Cinereous vulture
nodes.desc: Eats mostly carrion. The reserve is the only place in Armenia where it is known to nest, on juniper trees.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: The only bird that lives mostly on bones, dropping large ones from the air to break them open.

nodes.name: Persian leopard
nodes.desc: A big cat of the Caucasus mountains and a predator of wild goats and boar.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter that takes hares, wild ungulates and smaller prey in the reserve.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: The largest predator of the reserve, though most of a brown bear diet is plants such as fruit and acorns.
